correctness.rationale: For integers d>=2,C>=2,N>=2d with disjoint d-point endpoint stencils, exact integer Lagrange coefficients at extrapolation distance q have absolute values binom(q+j-1,j)binom(q+d-1,d-1-j). Their sum Lambda_d(q) is strictly increasing. As the left and right stencils are disjoint, a positive blended row has exact l_infinity coefficient norm (1-sigma(q/C))Lambda_d(q)+sigma(q/C)Lambda_d(C-q), and the operator norm is the maximum row norm. At even C=2k the center q=k gives Lambda_d(k); at odd C=2k+1 strict increase forces a strictly larger row because sigma(k/C)>0. The smooth polynomial symmetric beta-CDF family concentrating at 1/2 converges to a step, so the inf is Lambda_d(k); for even C strict positive gaps at all off-center rows imply finite m attains the center minimum, for odd C it cannot be attained. Leading binomial coefficient gives C^(d-1)/(d-1)!+O(C^(d-2)); keeping original data adds an identity block of norm one and does not change the result. The N>=2d restriction and endpoint derivative flatness are essential.

value.rationale: Provides an exact conditioning obstruction of a concrete smooth extrapolation-based Fourier continuation algorithm, including a phase distinction between attainment and strict unattainability and a high-degree growth law. This distinguishes arbitrary input noise from smooth-data approximation error and identifies a useful, unavoidable worst-case design limit.

limitations: Worst-case perturbation operator in l_infinity, not FFT approximation accuracy, spectral differentiability, floating-point recurrence errors or structured smooth noise.
